newsitem.title: USA: Coke has $50 mln ad deal with CBS -- report.
newsitem.headline: Coke has $50 mln ad deal with CBS -- report.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co has struck a $50 million deal with Westinghouse Electric Corp's CBS television under which the beverage giant will be the exclusive soft-drink advertiser for the 1998 Winter Olympics, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution newspaper reported Tuesday.

It said the agreement also covers ads on other CBS sports and entertainment programs from October 1997 through September 1998, including "The Late Show with David Letterman" and "The Country Music Awards."
Coca-Cola had no immediate comment on the report.
The newspaper said the deal was part of Coca-Cola's growing emphasis on television programs as a vehicle for promotion.
The newspaper quoted a Coca-Cola spokesman as saying the company was increasing advertising purchases on CBS because of steps the network has taken to strengthen its schedule.
The spokesman said Coca-Cola also would look at opportunities with Walt Disney Co's ABC, General Electric Co's NBC, and Rupert Murdoch's Fox network.

In May Coca-Cola plans a promotion in which the season finale of the NBC situation comedy "3rd Rock From The Sun" would be shown in 3-D. The glasses to watch the show will be given away with Coke's Barq's brand root beer.
